title: DNS, Ingress and Gateway API

header.html: Understand and use CoreDNS; Know how to use Ingress controllers and Ingress resources; Use the Gateway API to manage Ingress traffic

Kubernetes v1.37.0, CoreDNS from the kubeadm default, Traefik as Ingress controller and Gateway API implementation, Gateway API CRDs v1.6.3 (standard channel). The exam may use a different controller (for example NGINX); the Kubernetes objects are the same, only the class names differ.

toc.title: Ingress: HTTP routing into the cluster
Gateway API: the successor to Ingress

html:
1CoreDNS

CoreDNS is the cluster DNS server. It runs as a Deployment (2 replicas) in kube-system, behind the Service kube-dns whose ClusterIP is the nameserver in every Pod's /etc/resolv.conf (Lab 8.1).

What Where
Pods k get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns
Service k get svc -n kube-system kube-dns
Configuration ConfigMap coredns, key Corefile

The default Corefile is a list of plugins inside a server block .:53 { ... }:

Plugin Job
kubernetes cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa answers Service and Pod names of the cluster
forward . /etc/resolv.conf sends everything else to the upstream resolver (Lab 8.2)
cache 30 caches answers
errors, health, ready, prometheus, loop, reload, loadbalance logging, probes, metrics, safety, auto-reload
hosts { ... } extra static name to IP entries (you add this; Lab 8.3)

Change the configuration (Lab 8.3): edit the ConfigMap, then restart CoreDNS so the new Corefile is loaded at once:

k -n kube-system edit configmap coredns          # add:   hosts { 10.1.2.3 app.corp.local   fallthrough }   before the forward line
k -n kube-system rollout restart deployment coredns
k -n kube-system rollout status deployment coredns
k run t --rm -i --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -- nslookup app.corp.local

(reload also reloads the file after a while, but restarting is deterministic.) fallthrough inside hosts lets other names continue down the plugin chain; without it only your entries would resolve.

Records you get for free:

Name Answer
<svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local Service ClusterIP (headless: the Pod IPs)
<pod-ip-dashed>.<ns>.pod.cluster.local Pod IP
<pod>.<headless-svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local StatefulSet Pod IP

When DNS fails: CoreDNS Pods Running? k logs of CoreDNS shows config errors ("Unknown directive"); Pod dnsPolicy; the kube-dns endpoints (Modules 8.4, 13.5, 13.6).

2Ingress: HTTP routing into the cluster

An Ingress is a set of HTTP(S) routing rules (host and path to a Service). It does nothing alone: an Ingress controller (a Deployment running a reverse proxy such as NGINX or Traefik) watches Ingress objects and configures itself. Check what is installed:

k get ingressclass                         # classes available; the default has an annotation
k get pods -A | grep -i -E "ingress|traefik"
k get svc -A | grep -i -E "ingress|traefik"

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata: {name: routes, namespace: ing1}
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik                 # which controller handles it
  rules:
  - host: a.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix                    # Prefix, Exact or ImplementationSpecific
        backend:
          service: {name: a, port: {number: 80}}
  tls:                                      # optional: HTTPS
  - hosts: [secure.example.com]
    secretName: web-tls                     # a kubernetes.io/tls Secret in the same namespace

Imperative: k create ingress routes --class=traefik --rule="a.example.com/*=a:80" --rule="b.example.com/*=b:80" -n ing1 (a trailing /* makes a Prefix path). Generate and edit with --dry-run=client -o yaml.

Field Meaning
ingressClassName picks the controller; a missing or wrong class means nobody serves the Ingress (Lab 8.7)
host match the HTTP Host header; omit for any host
path + pathType Prefix matches /a and /a/b; Exact matches only that path
backend.service a Service in the same namespace and its port (number or name)
defaultBackend where unmatched requests go
tls terminate HTTPS with the Secret's certificate

Test without DNS by sending the Host header to the controller's Service:

k run t --rm -i --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -- wget -qO- -T3 --header "Host: a.example.com" http://<controller-svc>.<ns>

Common faults: wrong ingressClassName; backend Service name or port wrong (typically a 404/502); Service has no endpoints (Module 13); backend in another namespace (not allowed); missing TLS Secret.

3Gateway API: the successor to Ingress

The Gateway API splits the job into roles and is more expressive than Ingress. It is a set of CRDs plus an implementation (a controller); it is allowed in the exam (documentation at gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io).

Object Owner Job
GatewayClass infrastructure provider names an implementation (like an IngressClass)
Gateway cluster operator a listener: port, protocol, which routes may attach
HTTPRoute application developer rules: hostnames, matches (path, headers), backends (with weights), filters 
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: web-gw, namespace: gw1}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: traefik                # from `k get gatewayclass`
  listeners:
  - name: http
    protocol: HTTP
    port: 8000                             # must match a port the implementation listens on
    allowedRoutes: {namespaces: {from: Same}}
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: routes, namespace: gw1}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: web-gw}]             # attach to the Gateway
  hostnames: [a.example.com]
  rules:
  - matches: [{path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}}]
    backendRefs: [{name: a, port: 80}]     # add `weight:` to split traffic

Check: k get gatewayclass,gateway,httproute -A; k describe gateway web-gw and k describe httproute routes show conditions (Accepted, Programmed, ResolvedRefs) that tell you why a route is not working. Typical faults: wrong gatewayClassName; listener port or protocol mismatch; parentRefs pointing at the wrong Gateway name or namespace; backendRefs to a missing Service or wrong port; a route in another namespace when allowedRoutes says Same.

In the lab cluster: Traefik's HTTP entry point listens on container port 8000 (its Service forwards port 80 to it), so the Gateway listener uses port: 8000; the IngressClass traefik is marked as the default class and the GatewayClass traefik shows ACCEPTED True. Another implementation may use different ports and class names: always read k get gatewayclass,ingressclass and the controller's documentation first.

Ingress versus Gateway API in one line: Ingress = one object, HTTP only, behavior via controller annotations; Gateway API = role-separated objects, richer matching and traffic splitting, portable.

4Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m08 -->

Lab 8.1: dns server ip

Domain: Networking | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m08-01-dns-server-ip)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Pods in the cluster send their DNS queries to the cluster DNS Service. Find the IP address that a Pod uses as its nameserver (the nameserver line in /etc/resolv.conf inside a Pod) and write only that IP to ~/answers/dns-ip.txt on the host. Confirm that it is the ClusterIP of the DNS Service.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n kube-system get svc kube-dns
kubectl run dnsip --rm -i --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -q -- cat /etc/resolv.conf
kubectl -n kube-system get svc kube-dns -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}' > ~/answers/dns-ip.txt

Lab 8.2: coredns upstream

Domain: Networking | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m08-02-coredns-upstream)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

CoreDNS forwards names that are not in the cluster to an upstream resolver. Read the CoreDNS configuration (the Corefile in the ConfigMap coredns in kube-system) and write the upstream that the forward . line points to (for example /etc/resolv.conf or an IP) to ~/answers/upstream.txt.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n kube-system get configmap coredns -o jsonpath='{.data.Corefile}' | grep -n forward
kubectl -n kube-system get configmap coredns -o jsonpath='{.data.Corefile}' | awk '$1=="forward"{print $3}' > ~/answers/upstream.txt

Lab 8.3: coredns custom host

Domain: Networking | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m08-03-coredns-custom-host)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Make every Pod in the cluster resolve the name app.corp.local to the IP address 10.1.2.3 by changing the CoreDNS configuration. Keep all existing settings. After the change, CoreDNS must be running again (restart it so the new Corefile is loaded). Hint: the hosts plugin maps names to IPs. A new block goes before the forward line.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n kube-system get configmap coredns -o jsonpath='{.data.Corefile}' > /tmp/Corefile
sed -i 's#^    forward \. #    hosts {\n       10.1.2.3 app.corp.local\n       fallthrough\n    }\n    forward . #' /tmp/Corefile
kubectl -n kube-system create configmap coredns --from-file=Corefile=/tmp/Corefile --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment coredns
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deployment coredns --timeout=120s
kubectl run lookup --rm -i --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -q -- nslookup app.corp.local

Lab 8.4: fix dns down

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m08-04-fix-dns-down)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Name resolution inside the cluster has stopped: Pods cannot resolve kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local. Find out why and fix it so that name resolution works again and CoreDNS runs with its normal 2 replicas.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n kube-system get deployment coredns
kubectl -n kube-system get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=kube-dns
kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment coredns --replicas=2
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deployment coredns --timeout=120s

Lab 8.5: ingress host routing

Domain: Networking | Points: 8 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m08-05-ingress-host-routing)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

An Ingress controller (IngressClass traefik) runs in the cluster. In the namespace ing1, the Services a and b (port 80) exist. Create an Ingress named routes that uses the class traefik and sends requests for the host a.example.com to the Service a and requests for the host b.example.com to the Service b, for all paths.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl get ingressclass
kubectl -n ing1 create ingress routes --class=traefik --rule="a.example.com/*=a:80" --rule="b.example.com/*=b:80"
kubectl -n ing1 get ingress routes
sleep 5

Lab 8.6: ingress tls

Domain: Networking | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m08-06-ingress-tls)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace ing2, the Service a exists. A certificate and key for secure.example.com are in ~/answers/tls.crt and ~/answers/tls.key. Create a TLS Secret named web-tls from them, and an Ingress named secure (class traefik) that serves the host secure.example.com from the Service a on port 80 and uses the Secret for HTTPS.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n ing2 create secret tls web-tls --cert=$HOME/answers/tls.crt --key=$HOME/answers/tls.key
kubectl -n ing2 create ingress secure --class=traefik --rule="secure.example.com/*=a:80,tls=web-tls"
kubectl -n ing2 get ingress secure
sleep 5

Lab 8.7: fix ingress class

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m08-07-fix-ingress-class)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace ing3, the Ingress site for the host site.example.com (backend Service a) is not served: the controller answers 404. Find the cause and fix the Ingress (keep its name and rules) so that site.example.com returns the page of Service a.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl get ingressclass
kubectl -n ing3 get ingress site -o jsonpath='{.spec.ingressClassName}'; echo
kubectl -n ing3 patch ingress site --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"ingressClassName":"traefik"}}'
sleep 6

Lab 8.8: fix ingress backend

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m08-08-fix-ingress-backend)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace ing4, requests for shop.example.com through the Ingress shop fail. The Service web is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Ingress so that shop.example.com returns the page of the Service web.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n ing4 describe ingress shop | grep -i -A2 backend
kubectl -n ing4 get svc
kubectl -n ing4 patch ingress shop --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/rules/0/http/paths/0/backend/service/name","value":"web"}]'
sleep 6

Lab 8.9: gateway httproute

Domain: Networking | Points: 9 | Time: about 10 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m08-09-gateway-httproute)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The Gateway API is installed with the GatewayClass traefik. In the namespace gw1, the Service a (port 80) exists. Create a Gateway web-gw with one HTTP listener named http on port 8000 (class traefik, routes from the same namespace allowed), and an HTTPRoute route-a attached to it that sends the host a.example.com and all paths to the Service a on port 80.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl get gatewayclass
kubectl -n gw1 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: web-gw}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: traefik
  listeners:
  - name: http
    protocol: HTTP
    port: 8000
    allowedRoutes: {namespaces: {from: Same}}
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: route-a}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: web-gw}]
  hostnames: [a.example.com]
  rules:
  - matches: [{path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}}]
    backendRefs: [{name: a, port: 80}]
Y
sleep 8
kubectl -n gw1 get gateway,httproute

Lab 8.10: fix httproute

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 8 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m08-10-fix-httproute)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace gw2, the Gateway edge exists and the HTTPRoute route should send a.example.com to the Service a, but requests are not served. Use kubectl describe on the route to find the problem, and fix the HTTPRoute (keep its name).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n gw2 describe httproute route | grep -i -A6 "Parents"
kubectl -n gw2 get gateway
kubectl -n gw2 patch httproute route --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/parentRefs/0/name","value":"edge"}]'
sleep 8

Lab 8.11: httproute weights

Domain: Networking | Points: 8 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m08-11-httproute-weights)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace gw3, the Gateway edge, and the Services stable and canary (both port 80) exist. Create an HTTPRoute named split attached to edge that handles the host app.example.com and sends 90% of the traffic to the Service stable and 10% to the Service canary.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n gw3 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: split}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: edge}]
  hostnames: [app.example.com]
  rules:
  - backendRefs:
    - {name: stable, port: 80, weight: 90}
    - {name: canary, port: 80, weight: 10}
Y
sleep 8
kubectl -n gw3 get httproute split

<!-- /LABS -->

5Recall questions

R1Which ConfigMap holds the CoreDNS configuration and which key?

Show the answer

coredns in kube-system, key Corefile.

R2Which plugin forwards non-cluster names to an upstream resolver?

Show the answer

forward.

R3After editing the Corefile, how do you make CoreDNS load it right away?

Show the answer

kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment coredns.

R4An Ingress exists but nothing serves it. What do you check first?

Show the answer

That ingressClassName names an existing IngressClass whose controller is running (kubectl get ingressclass).

R5Can an Ingress route to a Service in another namespace?

Show the answer

No; the backend Service must be in the Ingress's namespace.

R6What are the three main Gateway API objects?

Show the answer

GatewayClass, Gateway and HTTPRoute.

R7How do you see why an HTTPRoute is not working?

Show the answer

kubectl describe httproute <name>: read the status conditions (Accepted, ResolvedRefs).

R8How do you test an Ingress rule for a host without changing DNS?

Show the answer

Send the request to the controller's Service with a Host: header.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
CoreDNS ConfigMap coredns (Corefile), Deployment in kube-system, restart after editing
Plugins kubernetes, forward, hosts (extra names, needs fallthrough), cache
Ingress needs a controller; ingressClassName, host, path + pathType, backend Service in the same namespace
Imperative k create ingress NAME --class= --rule="host/path=svc:port"
Gateway API GatewayClass -> Gateway (listener) -> HTTPRoute (parentRefs, hostnames, rules, backendRefs)
Debug describe shows conditions; test with a Host: header
